# sensors_plus, vendored for MotoCam

Upstream: sensors_plus 7.1.1 from pub.dev (pubspec.lock sha256 50a01f66846bff68de947bd5df225c3627c923c467f758867f3916350be059ac), copied unchanged except that `example/` is left out (commit "chore(deps): vendor sensors_plus 7.1.1 unchanged"). Used through `dependency_overrides` in the app's pubspec.yaml. sensors_plus_platform_interface stays the hosted 2.0.2. Licence: LICENSE in this folder (BSD-style).

Why vendored: on the test phone (vivo, Android 13) the accelerometer and linear-acceleration channels each deliver about 101 samples a second whatever period the app requests (20 ms for linear acceleration, 66.7 ms for the raw accelerometer), and upstream sends every sample as one main-thread platform message. Flutter 3.41 runs Dart on that same thread. In a traced 2160p60 debug run (2026-11-17, s9-trace-fix1, analysed 2026-11-19) the two channels took about 170 to 205 ms of main-thread CPU per second, the largest item on that thread (MotoCam-audit-data/2026-10-20/device-run-2026-11-10/analysis/s11-mainload).

## Patches

1. Slow streams are averaged on a background thread (`android/.../StreamHandlerImpl.kt`, `SensorsPlugin.kt`, new `BlockAverager.kt`). A stream whose requested sampling period is 50 ms or longer (`SensorInterval.uiInterval`, `normalInterval`) registers its `SensorEventListener` on a plugin `HandlerThread` ("SensorsPlus", display priority, started on first use and quit on engine detach after the streams are cancelled). There `BlockAverager` averages every sample of each period (phase-locked to the period on the sensor clock, so the output rate equals the requested rate; a block-closing sample more than half a period late, after a gap in the source, restarts the schedule, so outputs stay at least about half a period apart) and the mean, stamped with the block's last sensor timestamp, is posted to the main thread, where `EventSink.success` must run (`FlutterJNI.dispatchPlatformMessage` throws off the main thread). Averaging, not keeping one sample in N: picking would alias vibration into the result (in simulation, false tip-over confirmations under 2 to 4 g vibration near 15, 30 or 45 Hz). Shorter periods (`gameInterval`, `fastestInterval`, the `SENSOR_DELAY_*` constants) keep the upstream listener on the main looper and deliver every sample. On unregister (cancel or a period change) the listener is marked inactive on the main thread, and a sample it posted before that is dropped. Event format, timestamps, the Dart side and iOS are unchanged. In MotoCam this cuts the orientation stream (raw accelerometer at `uiInterval`) from about 101 to 15 main-thread messages a second; the linear-acceleration stream (20 ms) and the gravity fallback's raw stream (20 ms), which feed the jolt detector, are untouched. Tests: `BlockAveragerTest` (JVM: 100.9 and 200 Hz sources give 15 Hz, a 50 Hz square wave averages out, a slower source passes through, a long gap resyncs without a burst, gaps of 4 to 14 missing samples give no short catch-up block, a clock going back does not stall output); run with `android/gradlew :sensors_plus:testDebugUnitTest` from the app. Phone check (passed 2026-11-19 on a debug build of this patch plus the diag logs, whose crash debug log adds the per-second `grav` vector; a traced 2160p60 run and a tilt run, results in the project's device-run notes, "Session 11 run"): a traced 2160p60 run shows about 15 sends a second on `dev.fluttercommunity.plus/sensors/accelerometer` and about 101 on `.../user_accel`, no FlutterJNI RuntimeException, the crash debug log's per-second linear sample count still about 101, and its `grav` vector still follows the phone's tilt.

## Upgrading

Copy the new release over this folder (leave out `example/`), reapply the patch above, run `android/gradlew :sensors_plus:testDebugUnitTest` from the app and the app's checks, and repeat the phone check.
